overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: a revised tax option not anticipated by the chair 48 hours ahead could be discussed, and the Charter-based claim was declined as outside OML review. Concern noted, no order.

allegations.summary: Council discussed and voted on a revised tax option (appropriating $3.7M free cash) at its Dec 5, 2016 meeting though it was not on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find that to be the case here where Mayor Koch formulated an alternate tax proposal after being approached by individual Council members over the weekend and then presented such proposal to the Council after it had convened its December 5 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the Council could not approve the $3.7M appropriation under the City Charter because it was not duly noticed.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law allows a public body to discuss a topic that was not listed on a meeting notice if that topic was not reasonably anticipated by the chair 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
